After the Colonel's panther mask speech, Barnes wonders what kind of fucked up shit he's been drinking.

The next morning, Barnes is stretching and talking to Daniels by the campfire. Later, he cuts and opens the chainlink on the fence for Beard. After taking the plant, Barnes is trying to pick the lock on the control room door, before the Russian General kills all the engineers and himself and sends the plant into meltdown. Barnes and Jacket run over to the elevators, and Barnes reaches them first. The elevator explodes and blows most of Barnes' right half and face off, and he appears to be screaming. Daniels rushes over to comfort his friend in his last moments as the plant explodes.

characters.name: Mike Dalton
characters.desc: Mikes first appearance was in the Hotline Miami Wildlife comics issue #3 during February 10th 1989 in his store. From what was in the issue he was recruited by the 50 Blessings for killing the two Russians in his convenience store after they asked for his "Protection money." The protection money they were speaking of was probably some kind of fee he was paying the Russians to protect him. It's never mentioned what the money was protecting him from but since they threatened him it was most likely to protect him from being killed by them.

p: Mikes first appearance was in the Hotline Miami Wildlife comics issue #3 during February 10th 1989 in his store. From what was in the issue he was recruited by the 50 Blessings for killing the two Russians in his convenience store after they asked for his "Protection money." The protection money they were speaking of was probably some kind of fee he was paying the Russians to protect him. It's never mentioned what the money was protecting him from but since they threatened him it was most likely to protect him from being killed by them.
After Mike was recruited by the 50 Blessings just like any other member of the group he was assigned places to go and kill Russians. The dates of which the killings took place are;

Throughout the 3rd issue of the Hotline Miami Wildlife comics Mike is seen to be very smug and proud of himself. Mike often talks about himself in a very prideful way. During the panels when Aleksei was talking to Mike it is shown that Mike belittles the mobster acting as if he is a moron for not knowing how he would have to join and the requirements he would have to meet.

characters.name: Chris Jenkins
characters.desc: Chris Jenkins is the main protagonist of the Hotline Miami: Wildlife comics

p: Chris is a college student and one day, while taking cocaine and hanging out with his girlfriend, he gets a package full of weapons and a bunny mask. When he refuses to show his girlfriend what is in the package, she gets mad at him and leaves.

Chris is later tempted and does what the phone calls tell him to do. Along the way, he finds a kid named Peter who says that he hates how the Russians have been treating him and he wants Chris to help him.
This is a compiled list of how many kills Chris Jenkins has performed in the series:
About 36 Russian Mobsters (Shared with Aleksei)

characters.name: Kurt
characters.death: Unknown (might have gotten killed by Chris Jenkins or the nuke)
characters.desc: This is a compiled list of how many kills Kurt has performed in the series. Kills in Vietnam War are ambiguous due to that weren't show, so won't be take in count.

p: This is a compiled list of how many kills Kurt has performed in the series. Kills in Vietnam War are ambiguous due to that weren't show, so won't be take in count.

characters.name: Aleksei
characters.death: Unknown (either alive or killed by the Russian mob, the police or the nuke)
characters.desc: Aleksei is a Russian mobster defector and a recurring character of the Hotline Miami: Wildlife comics.

p: The first appearance of Aleksei was Hotline Miami Wildlife Issue #3 Every appearance from then are;

Aleksei was first introduced after Mike Dalton's rampage on April 3rd 1989. Aleksei killed his boss and proposed an question to Mike. He asked if he could join the 50 Blessings since he came to America to live not to be a part of the Russian Mafia. Mike laughed in his face explaining he couldn't just join. On top of that he told him even if he met the requirements he's a Russian, they'd kill him the first chance they got. Aleksei, upset with this answer, killed Mike taking his mask, and taking his place.
This is a compiled list of how many kills Aleksei has performed in the series:
About 36 Russian Mobsters (Shared with Chris Jenkins)
Aleksei is shown to be a remorseless cold-hearted killer. Proof of this is shown in Issue #4 where he shows little to no remorse after possibly killing several children.

characters.name: Peter
characters.desc: Peter is a recurring character of the Hotline Miami: Wildlife comics.

p: In Issue #1 of the Hotline Miami Wildlife comics he was introduced as a survivor of Chris Jenkins rampage. Later in issue #2 It's revealed that he's the son of a Russian Mobster (Later killed by Wilson Barnes). During issue #2 he's taken into the care of Chris Jenkins.

characters.name: Tattoo Artist
characters.desc: The Tattoo Artist, possibly also known as the Tension Man or Tony , is a minor character in Hotline Miami (possibly) and Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. He is seen in the outro of Hard News.

p: He may or may not be Russian, as he is called a "Russian asshole" (presumably by not getting his way) by Jake. His name may also be Tony (not to be confused with The Fan member Tony), as the tattoo parlor logo is "Tony Skate Tattoo".

He schedules Jake's appointment "next Friday at 2 PM," which is the date of Tension, May 5th, 1989. This could indicate he's the 50 Blessings member wearing a Tony Mask in that level, if so he is killed by Jacket, who blasts the door open with a shotgun, causing the entire room to explode. (But this theory is sketchy at best as it's possible that he's just a business owner. There is no actual evidence to link the "Tony" mask to this character aside from the tattoo parlor's logo.)

characters.name: Manager
characters.desc: The Manager is a side character and an antagonist in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. He is a man who appears at the beginning of Withdrawal and a second time if you manage to not die as Jake on the 3rd floor of Withdrawal. He is the main antagonist of Jake's storyline.

p: The Manager appears to work in a large lead-lined office building in Miami, seemingly being in charge of the branch. As manager, he cordially welcomes prospective members with a broad smile and has an open ear for any suggestions to help advance their cause. He drops his friendly act however, when pressed about anything relating to odd phone calls or violence, becoming very adamant that their group is pacifist and non-coercive, consistently denying any involvement and claiming to have no idea what Jake is talking about when he unwittingly proposes and describes to him the exact operation they are already running.

The building Jake meets him in is a reinforced 50 Blessings center (which is the setting of The Abyss later), with the implication that he very well could be the leader, or at the very least a high-ranking executive, of the 50 Blessings operation. At the time, it was being run as a non-profit organization as a front, a fact Jake found out by chance and had to pay the price for.

characters.name: Colombian Boss
characters.desc: The Colombian Boss is a minor character and an antagonist during the final act of Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. He is the head boss of the Colombian Cartel, and one of the only two notable Colombian characters in the game. He is accompanied by a man with two guard dogs. Although he only appears once in the whole game, he is The Son's rival and nemesis, and serves as the main antagonist of his storyline.

story.h: Events of Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number
p: During an unknown period between the end of Hotline Miami and somewhere before the events of Hotline Miami 2, the Colombian Boss and the rest of his cartel claim property owned by the Russian Mafia after the death of the then boss of the Mafia in 1989, and use the Russian's property for their own business.

Two years later in 1991, The Son (the current boss of the Russian Mafia) has held a grudge on the Colombians ever since. After being given an invitation to a Colombian-owned strip club, The Son speaks with The Henchman over this matter and declares war on the Colombians, stating that there would never be a better time. He starts the war with the Colombians by attacking the strip club on his own.

characters.name: Van Driver
characters.desc: The Van Driver, or Molotov Guy, is a character and an antagonist in Hotline Miami. He serves as the boss enemy of Part Three: Visitations, where he is encountered at the end of Chapter 11, Deadline.

p: He drives through the main doors with his van, some mobsters and thugs come out of the vehicle and start to attack Jacket while the van's driver throws Molotov cocktails at the masked murderer.

After killing all the thugs and mobsters from the van, the driver will surrender. Jacket beats him to death with his bare hands - smashing his head against the floor and breaking a number of his bones - and then lights his corpse on fire. This execution has bursts of dream static, and the driver noticeably looks like a nonsensical blend of Richter and Biker, hinting that Jacket didn't really brutally kill the driver and is just dreaming a cathartic revenge on those characters he failed to kill.

characters.name: Zombie Russian
characters.desc: The Zombie Russian is an NPC who appears in the outro of Chapter Nine, Crackdown. He stands outside the pizzeria with Parker, aggressively warning Jacket that his presence isn't welcome. Like the other undead mobsters, he is covered in blood and has been horrifically maimed, having had his lower jaw ripped out.

characters.name: The Bodyguard
characters.desc: The Bodyguard, also known as the Ninja Girl, is a character and a boss in Hotline Miami and a posthumous minor character in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. She served as The Father's primary bodyguard during 1989 and had a vague relationship with The Son, who seems to keep her smashed sunglasses and katana in 1991. She is the penultimate boss of Hotline Miami.

p: The Bodyguard is the second boss fought in Chapter 15, Showdown, with the first boss fight being the two panthers. She uses throwing knives at range and an Iaijutsu strike with her katana at close quarters. Both attacks will instantly kill Jacket, and are extremely difficult to dodge.

After Jacket kills the panthers, the Bodyguard taunts him and the fight will commence. The only weapon of choice is the trophy that Jacket still holds firmly, fresh with panther blood. Do not attempt to melee the Bodyguard with the trophy, because it will have no effect and her katana will kill you in one hit.

To defeat the Bodyguard, the player must knock her down by throwing the trophy and then jumping on top of her for an execution move. The best way to perform this maneuver is right after her dialog finishes, as she will run straight towards Jacket. If the player is outside of the battle arena after killing the panthers, she will throw a knife, resulting in immediate death. A common strategy is to lock on to her while hiding from the panthers. Defeat the panthers, step into sight and throw the trophy- make sure you're standing still when you throw it.

In Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, she appears at the end of Blood Money, alongside The Father and The Grandfather. She alongside the two are encountered by The Son as a hallucination, showing that he sees the Bodyguard as a part of his family. After The Son has a conversation with his father, the Bodyguard will grab a Richard mask and pull it over The Grandfather's head, which summons Richard to converse with The Son.
Unlike The Father, the Bodyguard and the Grandfather do not speak a single line of dialogue during their brief reappearance.
Picking up a throwing star before the phone rings will result in it turning into a scissor.

characters.name: The Producer
characters.desc: Wilson Fisker, better known as The Producer, is an antagonist in Hotline Miami. He is an "adult" movie producer with ties to the Russian Mafia, and the boss of Part One: Phone Calls, making him the first boss enemy the player encounters. His playstyle sets the precedent for and introduces the player to the generic thugs to be encountered later on. The Producer is found at the end of Chapter 3, Decadence, on the first floor after every other enemy has been killed. He can be seen beforehand in his room looking at a set of screens eating popcorn, presumably watching Jacket's murder spree through the security cameras scattered about the level, much like a slasher flick. A heavily sedated girl lies on his bed surrounded by cameras. This room is inaccessible until the player clears out the second floor.

p: After Jacket clears out the first and second floors of the building, the Producer will leave his previously locked room and attempt to beat Jacket to death.

The Producer will not take damage from anything except shotguns. Upon being hit by a shotgun blast, he will be knocked off his feet and lay on the ground stunned for a few seconds before continuing pursuit. Once the player has knocked the Producer off his feet for the third time, or if they run up at him immediately after he has been knocked down the second time, the player can perform a gruesome execution on him, gouging his eyes out with their thumbs.

characters.name: Phantom
characters.desc: Phantom, also known as Ventriloquist, is a minor character and an antagonist in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. He is a strange entity that confronts Manny Pardo in a nightmare he has.

p: Phantom appears in Pardo's nightmare, who keeps hold of the revolver Pardo leaves behind at one of the "Miami Mutilator's" crime scenes. Pardo insists on knowing what Phantom is doing at the crime scene, to which he responds "Well, you know what they say...Murderers always return to the scene of the crime."

Pardo then asks who Phantom is, who responds with that he could think of him as his son and that he was created by Pardo. The shaken Detective rudely asks for his gun back. Phantom offers Pardo a "hug" and begins to strangle him. After a short struggle, the detective retaliates by pushing him over. Phantom's head then smashes into pieces after hitting the floor, apparently killing him.

characters.name: Russian General
characters.desc: The Russian General is a minor character briefly seen in the Casualties scene of Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. He is the main antagonist of Beard's missions, shown operating out of a power plant in the volcanic region of Hawaii on October 30th, 1985.

story.h: Events of Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number
p: The Russian General appears to be the commander of the Soviet forces Beard's Unit has faced up to that point. He personally oversees the war in Hawaii from a large and extremely well fortified Power Plant. Much like his American counterpart, the Russian General appears to be losing his sanity and grip on reality as the war progresses.

After Beard's Unit takes the plant, Beard meets up with Daniels, Jacket, and Barnes. Barnes is attempting to pick the lock on the door to the main control room of the plant. Daniels comments that the Russian leader has "completely lost it", and the camera pans to reveal the bullet-ridden corpses of the power plant engineers at their stations, with the Russian General putting the final round in his head.

characters.name: Prison Boss
characters.death: Dead (bludgeoned over the head with a pipe)
characters.desc: The Prison Boss is character and an antagonist featured in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, where he is a minor boss character that appears in Act 5 Scene 4, Release. He is a 50 Blessings assassin in prison hired by the Janitors, tasked to kill Richter to tie up loose ends. However, he fails his mission in the ensuing riot, being killed by his target. Optional dialogue between a prison guard and Richter reveals that the guards were most likely bribed by the Janitors to force Richter to fight the inmate during lunch time, intending to have Richter killed in the process.

p: After threatening Richter he will begin walking towards him and occasionally begin charging similar to a charging inmate. Instead of using a punch to kill the player, he will do a Headbutt Execution if close enough.
After he charges at Richter twice, a cheering prisoner holding a Big Pipe will throw it into the court and this must be used to kill the Prison Boss and proceed to the next area.
This boss can be beaten by circling around him when he charges, as he doesn't turn as fast as you due to inertia.

characters.name: Gang Leader
characters.death: Dead (Either killed by an aggressive Evan or killed in an atomic blast if dealt with passively)
characters.desc: The Gang Leader is character and an antagonist featured in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, where he is a minor boss that appears in Act 4 Scene 1, Subway.

p: Upon entering the third area, he will be seen spray painting (Assumed to be their gang mark) over a subway map and will say "Heh, heh, heh. This is our turf now, boys! Let's tear it up!"

He will then begin to patrol the area on a set path. If Evan is seen by the leader at any point, he will begin hitting his Pipe on the ground signaling most of the punks to where you were spotted in an attempt to overwhelm the player.

characters.name: Pizza Dude
characters.desc: Enjoy your meal, and watch out for ghosts tonight, OK? Pizza Dude, also known as the Pizza Guy or the Cashier, is a minor character in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

p: On Halloween, 1991, he charges Mark $14.50 for several pizzas. Seeing that Mark's apparently in Halloween costume, he jokingly warns him to look out for spooky ghosts. His face is covered in pimples, a gag on his profession.

characters.name: Bum
characters.desc: Bum is a minor character featured in both Hotline Miami and Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. He first appears in Hotline Miami as an antagonist and enemy, and returns in a cameo appearance in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. He gets the first lines of dialogue in the series during Hotline Miami's tutorial. He teaches the player the combat mechanics of the game, and is very rude and hasty with Jacket. Given that he was one of Jacket's first murder victims and how he vomits after killing Bum, it is possible that this is a manifestation of Jacket's guilt from killing Bum in his conscience during his coma dream in the first half of the game, where Jacket relives the events of his life up until Richter's murder of his girlfriend and attempted murder of him afterwards.

p: He is encountered first as the narrator for the game's tutorial and then as an enemy at the end of Metro. Once Jacket has dropped off the briefcase in the dumpster, Bum will stand at the entrance of the alleyway with a baseball bat. Jacket must bash Bum's head in to advance, prompting him to remove his mask and vomit.

Bum reappears as a posthumous cameo appearance in the Bar of Broken Heroes in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, where he is seen rummaging through dumpster outside the bar. He cannot be interacted with by Evan.

characters.name: Technician
characters.desc: The Technician, is a minor character in Hotline Miami. He was hired by the Janitors to set up the phonelines in Phone Hom linking to the Russian club managed by The Club Owner.

p: He was scared by the political agenda of 50 Blessings, so he went into hiding inside a small Chinese restaurant called the Blue Dragon used as a safehouse. It's probable that he hired some Russian mobsters to protect him. The Charlie Mask is in his safehouse. He was isolated and paranoid until Biker came looking for him following a hint by Aubrey, and questioned him about the phone calls. It's unknown what happen to him after that.

characters.name: Courthouse Judge
characters.desc: The Courthouse Judge is a minor character in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. The Judge appears only once at the intro of First Trial. He adjourns court for the day after Lawyer and Prosecutor finish cross examining the Police Chief.

characters.name: Lawyer
characters.desc: The Lawyer is a minor character in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. He is Jacket's defense attorney during First Trial on November 5th, 1991.

story.h: Events in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number
p: Lawyer is apparently not Jacket's first attorney, as Jacket is apparently talking to a brown-haired attorney in the intro to Release on July 20th, 1990.

In First Trial, Lawyer cross examines the Police Chief, who has said there's no physical evidence supporting Jacket's claims. Lawyer asks if the police examined Jacket's phone records, which the Police Chief confirms. Lawyer then asks if the records match up with the time frame of Jacket's story, which the Chief also confirms. Lawyer asks if they traced those calls, and the Chief replies that they came from a nightclub called The Golden Truckstop. Lawyer then elucidates that Jacket is claiming he was coerced by the Russian Mafia to perform his hits, and asks if there's any connection between the mafia and the club.

characters.name: Prosecutor
characters.desc: The Prosecutor is a minor character in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. He is the prosecuting attorney of Jacket's trial in First Trial.

story.h: Events of Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number
p: On November 5th, 1991, he is shown cross examining the Police Chief. He asks the Chief if the police investigated Jacket's answering machine to confirm or deny his claims of phone messages. The Chief responds that the tape of the machine had been removed (possibly by Richter, who is later shown to collect 50 Blessings tapes). After this, Prosecutor asks if there was any evidence of threatening phone calls, which the Chief denies. The Prosecutor then let's Lawyer cross examine the Chief.

characters.name: The Club Manager
characters.desc: The Club Manager is a minor character in Hotline Miami. He manages the Russian Mafia-owned nightclub in Vengeance.

p: The Club Manager is encountered in the third stage of the chapter in an office surrounded by armed enemies. After dispatching the enemies, Jacket is able to confront him. The Manager does not attack Jacket, though there is a Magnum visible in his open desk drawer. Instead, he surrenders immediately, offering Jacket the contents of the open safe in the office. He explains that he wants no trouble from Jacket, and that he is not the owner of the club and therefore not the man Jacket seeks. Intimidated by Jacket, he stumbles and falls to the floor in fear, eventually revealing the location of the Russian Mafia Headquarters as a poor attempt to save his own life.

characters.name: Rouven Blankenfeld (The Director)
characters.desc: Rouven Blankenfeld or The Director is a minor character in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. He appears on Midnight Animal and Final Cut. He is the screenwriter and director of the movie Midnight Animal, based on the 1989 masked Russian Mafia killings. He also appears in Manny Pardo's hallucinations and dreams in Homicide and Caught. In the Midnight Animal intro to Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, he berates Martin Brown and Rachael Ward for not playing their characters archetypal enough, urging Martin to be rougher and Rachael to act more scared and helpless.

characters.name: Hobo
characters.desc: Hobo, also known as Chicken Hobo, is a minor character in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. He appears in the intros to two of Evan Wright's three missions, Subway and The Abyss. This mysterious character whose motives and positions are unclear appears to be affiliated with 50 Blessings in some way, although how exactly is unclear and never explained.

p: Hobo seems to have an aversion for Evan, from whom he denies his money offer despite being poor. He is later seen squatting in the abandoned 50 Blessings HQ, although it is unknown if this is an appearance seen in a hallucination or if he was actually there wearing the Richard mask.

Evan hallucinates and sees Richard speaking to him by through Hobo putting the rooster mask on, and later takes off the mask and reveals the head of Evan's wife, saying she's going to leave him, take the kids, and that he needs a real job outside of being a writer. Evan later snaps back to reality only to see Hobo tell him that he does not want his "stinking money". It is possible that during the hallucination, Evan was visibly behaving strangely as a result of his visions, which may have freaked out Hobo and made him not want to speak with Evan just to get some pocket change.

Hobo first appears in Subway. He is wandering inside a subway car where he meets Evan and asks him for money. Evan uncomfortably hands forth some money, but Hobo suddenly puts a Richard mask on his head; Evan is granted with a visit from Richard, who tells him if he looked like he wanted his "dirty money".

Evan expresses confusion, to which Hobo takes off the mask, revealing the face of Sharon, Evan's wife, instead of his own. Sharon explains to Evan his family situation and how his own job is gradually conflicting with their life. Evan reassures her that his book will be successful and insists that he just needs more time. Hobo once again dons the mask, and Richard tells Evan that he will never have enough time and advises that he reconsider his priorities.

In the secret level The Abyss, Hobo appears once again in the former 50 Blessings HQ, which now serves as a fallout bunker. He is sitting in a room wearing a Richard mask among other squatters wearing various animal masks. The hobos mistake Evan for someone else who had supposedly come to evict them and menacingly tell him to leave.
It is unclear if this scene was real or if it was merely a hallucination by Evan. Therefore, if Hobo really was in the fallout shelter, he could have survived the nuclear blast.

weapons.name: 9mm
weapons.desc: If you are looking for the unusable Desert Eagle in Hotline Miami's finale, see Pistol. The 9mm is a weapon in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. There is a silenced version of this weapon.

p: The 9mm is the second most common firearm in the game, being used by Gangsters, Miami's Police Force and being Ash Davis' weapon of choice. It has also seen use by the Soviet Dodgers, which dual-wield the pistol. However, Beard is unable to pick up the 9mm from fallen Dodgers. This is the weapon used by Rachael Ward to kill the Pig Butcher in Final Cut. The 9mm is functionally identical to the Silenced Pistol, albeit it lacks the silencer and it possesses a slightly larger magazine size. This weapon is required for the A BOX FULL OF SHARP OBJECTS achievement.

There is an accuracy discrepancy between the 9mm's accuracy when used by enemies versus player characters. When shot by enemies the 9mm will always be highly accurate at range. When used by the player the 9mm will always be inaccurate. It is possible to use this to one's advantage as it makes 9mm enemies have predictable shot patterns that can be easily avoidable with strafing (though the player will inevitably get shot and die depending on their current Energy Points). Finally it is advisable to avoid using the 9mm if one has access to better options such as the Shotgun, or Uzi.

stats.Accuracy: Poor (when used by player), High (When used by Enemies)

weapons.name: Automatic Shotgun
weapons.desc: The Automatic Shotgun is a weapon available in the Super Carnage prototype. It is a fully automatic shotgun with a grey barrel and a wooden grip.

p: The Automatic Shotgun is one of the firearms available to the Player, The Player can select it by cycling through their selection by pressing Q or E. It has a superior rate of fire to the Double Barrel, but it has a tighter spread.

weapons.name: Baseball Bat
weapons.desc: The Baseball Bat is a weapon seen in Hotline Miami and Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, where it is among one of the most common and iconic melee weapons in the entire series.

p: In Hotline Miami, the Baseball Bat is one of the most common melee weapons, being found many times on the ground and on the hands of Mobsters. This weapon is required for the Always On Top and Knife For Pros achievements. This is the first weapon you pick up in the franchise, during the Tutorial.

In Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, the Baseball Bat shares many similarities with the bat from the first game, being commonly found on the ground and wielded by common enemies like gangsters and mobsters. This weapon is required for the A BOX FULL OF SHARP OBJECTS achievement.
Long attack animation that makes hitting multiple enemies with one swing easier
Large weapon sprite, which makes knocking down enemies by throwing the weapon less difficult Cons:

weapons.name: Baton
weapons.desc: The Baton or the Stick is a weapon that appears in Hotline Miami and Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. It is a Tonfa stick; a stick with a perpendicular handle attached a third of the way down the length of the stick.

p: In Hotline Miami, the Baton can only be found in Assault, being seen quite commonly as most police officers carry it around, the only foes not carrying it being the Police Chief and the Inspectors. The Baton functions exactly like the Knife, however it has its own execution animation. This weapon is required for the Always On Top and Knife For Pros achievements.

The Baton returns in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, where it is much more common, since it can be found being carried by the Miami Police Department, Guards and Prisoners. It remains unchanged from the first game except for some new execution animations for certain characters. This weapon is required for the A BOX FULL OF SHARP OBJECTS achievement.
Fast attack animation, meaning hitting multiple enemies will be more difficult

weapons.name: Beer Can
weapons.desc: The Beer Can is a weapon available exclusively in Hotline Miami. It is an unmarked green can, presumably of

p: The Beer Can is an unlockable weapon, meaning it will randomly spawn once unlocked; It is the 5th weapon you receive. This weapon is required for the Pitcher and I Got New Friends achievements.

weapons.name: Big Pipe
weapons.desc: The Big Pipe is a weapon found only in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. It is a big, curved lead pipe used as a bludgeoning tool.

p: This weapon is first seen in the hands of the Gang Leader in the Subway level. He will patrol the last zone of the level and bang the pipe on the ground if he spots Evan. This causes all of his goons to run to Evan's last known position. Despite this unique behaviour, the Gang Leader cannot hit Evan with his pipe. The Big Pipe is seen again in Release, where a bystander throws Richter the pipe during the Prison Boss fight; which the player needs to use in order to beat the Prison Boss. This weapon is required for the A BOX FULL OF SHARP OBJECTS achievement.
Extremely rare, Hotline Miami 2 exclusive

weapons.name: Brick
weapons.desc: The Brick is a weapon exclusive to Hotline Miami.

p: The Brick is an unlockable weapon, meaning it will randomly spawn once you have unlocked it. It is the 8th weapon you receive. This weapon is required for the Pitcher, Plain Luck, Two Birds With One Stone and I Got New Friends achievements.
Large amount of points per throw kill and execution

weapons.name: Briefcase
weapons.desc: The Briefcase is an unique weapon in Hotline Miami, It appears to be an all black case with unknown contents.

p: This weapon is only seen in The Metro, where it serves as the main objective. Jacket is instructed by 50 Blessings to go to the metro station and retrieve the briefcase from the Briefcase Man and a group of Mobsters. Once this is done, he is then instructed to drop it off at an unmarked dumpster, where a Bum attacks him. This weapon is required for the Always On Top and Knife For Pros achievements. The Briefcase cannot be dropped, and Jacket will only let go of it once he drops it off at the dumpster.

weapons.name: Butterfly Knife
weapons.desc: If you are looking for the original version of this weapon, see Knife. The Butterfly Knife, also known as the Balisong is a weapon seen exclusively in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

p: The Butterfly Knife is one of the most common melee weapons in the game, as it is commonly seen in the hands of Gang Members, Colombians and Mobsters. The Butterfly Knife is introduced with the 1991 Setting and is retroactively used to replace the Knife in the 1989 setting for Jake and Richter's levels. However, The Soldier still uses the original knife in his levels. This weapon is required for the A BOX FULL OF SHARP OBJECTS achievement.
Has a chance to kill enemies if thrown at them
Cannot be retrieved if the thrown knife kills an enemy

weapons.name: Chainlink
weapons.desc: The Chainlink is a weapon seen in Hotline Miami and Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

p: In Hotline Miami, the Chainlink is seen as an unusable weapon that appears in the epilogue of Tension. It is seen being wielded by a Mobster, threateningly swinging it around as he and two other Mobsters surround a man wearing a Dennis Mask. After speaking to Beard in his store, the Mobsters disappear and the man is shown dead. This is the only ever time where the Chainlink appears in the first game.

In Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, it is a common weapon exclusively used by the Gang enemies. It is one of the slower weapons in the game, having a swing rate similar to the Baseball Bat. This weapon is required for the A BOX FULL OF SHARP OBJECTS achievement.

weapons.name: Chainsaw
weapons.desc: The Chainsaw is a weapon in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

p: This is one of the only melee weapons that is able to kill all enemy types, such as Thugs and Dodgers.

The Chainsaw can appear as early as Down Under (if the Player is on Hard Mode), where it is being wielded by Gang dodgers, although the Player unable to pick the weapon up from fallen dodgers. Upon finishing Moving Up, The Swans are unlocked, and if the Player picks them, Alex Davis will be wielding the chainsaw. This weapon then appears in Subway, where it is again being wielded by Gang dodgers, Again, Evan Wright is unable to pick this weapon up from fallen dodgers. This weapon has some of the lengthiest execution animations in the game. The Chainsaw is required for the A BOX FULL OF SHARP OBJECTS and GOT YOUR BACK achievements.

weapons.name: Cleaver
weapons.desc: The Cleaver is a weapon in Hotline Miami and Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

p: It is one of the only two weapons that can be used by Biker, the other one being the Throwing Knives. It is a meat cleaver traditionally used to slice through thick meat and bones. Unlike other melee weapons, this weapon has a special property that allows it to kill Thugs.

In Hotline Miami the Cleaver first appears being used by Biker in Neighbors, during the Phone Hom section of the level. He uses the weapon to try and kill Jacket by lunging at him every few seconds, After two lunges, he throws it at Jacket as an alternative attack. If he misses, he will have to go retrieve it. While he is retrieving the Cleaver, the Player is free to approach and strike him.
Varying execution animations, with some taking longer than others

weapons.desc: The Crossbow can be seen in Jacket's Final Chapter in a glass case next to the Trophy Weapon.

stats.Found: Found in Glass Case in Showdown

weapons.name: Crowbar
weapons.desc: The Crowbar is a weapon seen only in Hotline Miami.

p: In Hotline Miami, this weapon is only seen in Full House, where it can be used as a melee weapon, but also as a means to open the sewer hatch behind the house on the first floor. Once used, the Player can descend into the sewer to encounter Jones and the Jones Mask. This weapon is required for the Always On Top, Knife For Pros and Sewer Alligator achievements.

weapons.name: Dart
weapons.desc: The Dart is a throwable weapon featured in Hotline Miami. It is a dart usually used for playing Darts, It has red fletching, a yellow shaft and a steel tip.

p: The Dart is an unlockable weapon, meaning it will only spawn once it has been unlocked. It is the 12th weapon you receive. You cannot kill enemies with this weapon, however it is possible to damage and execute enemies. If you throw the Dart at an enemy wielding a weapon, you get an additional 500 points (+500 per each enemy alerted) for boldness and the accolade "Big Balls" at the end of the level. It has an execution animation similar to the Scissors. This weapon is required for the Pitcher and I Got New Friends achievements.
Large amount of bonus points per execution
"Big Balls" accolade, extra points for throwing this weapon at armed enemies Cons:

weapons.name: Double Barrel
weapons.desc: The Double Barrel is a weapon appearing in both Hotline Miami and Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

p: In Hotline Miami, the Double Barrel is a very common firearm, as Mobsters frequently use it; however Mobsters wielding Double Barrels are less common than Mobsters with M16s and Shotguns. This weapon is very strong, as it fires 20-28 projectiles with a large spread per shell, and it has a very fast rate of fire; however it has a miniscule magazine size, so it is likely to be discarded quickly. Due to the fact it has the longest sprite out of all the common weapons, the Double Barrel is the easiest weapons to hit when thrown at enemies, meaning it may be useful when using the Jake Mask. This weapon is required for the Guns For Show achievement.

Here, the Double Barrel is now rarer due to the fact that it is exclusively used by Mobsters; however, on levels with Mobsters it appears as frequently as its Hotline Miami counterpart. This weapon remains unchanged from it's first iteration. The Aubrey Mask in the Level Editor gives Jacket the Double Barrel at the start of the level. This weapon is required for the A BOX FULL OF SHARP OBJECTS achievement.

weapons.name: Drill
weapons.desc: The Drill is a weapon in Hotline Miami and Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

p: In Hotline Miami, the Drill is only available to the Player if you use the Carl Mask. It is one of the only melee weapons in the game (alongside the Briefcase) that is unable to kill an enemy in a single strike, likely to encourage an executioner / sadist playstyle. This weapon is required for the Always On Top achievement.
In Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, the Drill is only available in the Level Editor as a weapon pickup, or by selecting the Carl Mask.

weapons.name: Fireaxe
weapons.desc: The Fireaxe is a weapon that appears in Hotline Miami and Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

p: In Hotline Miami, the Fireaxe is an unlockable weapon, meaning that it can spawn randomly in several levels once unlocked; It's the 14th weapon you receive. It is required for the Smell Something Burning, Always On Top, Knife For Pros and I Got New Friends achievements.

In Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, the Fireaxe is much rarer as it only appears naturally in a few maps, like the second floor of Demolition, being able to destroy the thin wooden walls on the second floor. It is also seen in Apocalypse, where it is hallucinated by The Son to be the weapon he killed Alex and Ash with while he was under the effects of a potent hallucinogenic drug. This weapon is required for the A BOX FULL OF SHARP OBJECTS achievement. The Fireaxe is the last weapon used in the series.
Very rare, being only guaranteed to spawn in a few levels

weapons.desc: The Frying Pan is a weapon that appears in Hotline Miami.

p: In Hotline Miami, this weapon can only spawn in predetermined locations and cannot be naturally used by enemies. This weapon is required for the Always On Top and Knife For Pros achievements. This weapon is commonly mistaken for the Pot.

weapons.name: Glass Bottle
weapons.desc: The Glass Bottle is a weapon available in Hotline Miami and Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

p: It is a green unmarked bottle (presumably the same brand as the Beer Can) that breaks upon hitting anything that isn't a common enemy.

In Hotline Miami, the Glass Bottle is an unlockable weapon, meaning it can spawn randomly once it is unlocked. It is the second weapon you receive. It cannot kill enemies by directly hitting them with a throw, but it has an unique execution. The Glass Bottle is a one-time use weapon — it will break both upon missing an enemy and after being used in an execution. This weapon is required for the Pitcher, Always On Top and I Got New Friends achievements.
Moderate swing speed (Hotline Miami 2) Cons:

weapons.desc: The Golf Club is a weapon seen in Hotline Miami and Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, where it is one of the most common weapons in the first game.

p: In Hotline Miami the Golf Club is amongst one of the most common melee weapons in the game, being wielded by Mobsters and commonly being found on the ground. This weapon is required for the Always On Top and Knife For Pros achievements. This weapon is often mistaken for the Lead Pipe due to their very similar appearances and execution animations.
In Chapter 7, Jacket must perform an unique execution on Biker with the Golf Club, by standing in the posture used for playing golf, and smashing Biker's head off with a single fatal swing.
Long attack animation that makes hitting multiple enemies with one swing easier
Large weapon sprite, which makes knocking down enemies by throwing the weapon less difficult Cons:

p: In Hotline Miami, the Hammer is an unlockable weapon, meaning it may spawn randomly once it is unlocked; It is the 7th weapon you receive. The Hammer can also be seen in the "Wear Something Fancy" Trailer. This weapon is required for the Pitcher, Plain Luck, Two Birds With One Stone and I Got New Friends achievements.

In Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, it can be seen in the Midnight Animal scene, where it is used as a melee weapon rather than a throwable weapon. It has the same swing rate as the Baseball Bat and it has a different execution to the one seen in the first game. It is also featured in the Level Editor. This weapon is required for the A BOX FULL OF SHARP OBJECTS and FOLLOW THE SCRIPT achievements.

weapons.name: Heavy Machine Gun
weapons.desc: The Heavy Machine Gun or the Big and Heavy, is a weapon featured in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. It is one of the three weapons that is exclusively available for The Soldier. It is an LMG based off of the M249 SAW.

p: The Heavy Machine Gun is seen exclusively in the Hawaiian Conflict, where it is one of the weapons The Soldier can use if the Player picks it at the start of a Soldier level; It is only available once Ambush is completed. The Colonel is also seen holding this weapon. It has the second highest ammunition count in the game (the highest being the Flamethrower) and is the third most accurate weapon (beaten by the Sniper Rifle and the Flamethrower). Once starting ammunition is depleted, ammunition pickups will only give 10 rounds. This weapon is required for the A BOX FULL OF SHARP OBJECTS achievement.

weapons.name: Kalashnikov
weapons.desc: The Kalashnikov (Russian: Калашников) is a weapon featured in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

p: In this game, the Kalashnikov is quite a common firearm, as it sees extensive use from the Russian Mafia, and the Red Army during the Hawaiian Conflict. Despite this, The Soldier is unable to use the weapon in his levels, although Barnes is seen using it in the level Casualties. The Kalashnikov is required for the A BOX FULL OF SHARP OBJECTS achievement. This weapon is very similar to the M16, but it has a slower rate of fire and is less accurate.

weapons.name: Katana
weapons.desc: The Katana or Samurai Sword is a weapon that appears in Hotline Miami and Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

p: In Hotline Miami, the Katana is an unlockable weapon, meaning it can spawn randomly once unlocked, It is the first weapon you receive. The Bodyguard is the only enemy in the game who wields the Katana. This weapon is required if you want to unlock the Always On Top, Knife For Pros and I Got New Friends achievements.

In Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, the Katana functions rather differently than it did in the first game. When used, the Katana is kept sheathed inside a sword scabbard, and is unsheathed when the player attacks before being sheathed again, similarly to how the Bodyguard attacks with her Katana in the first game; meaning the weapon attacks slower in this game. The Katana is used by The Son (if the Bodyguard Technique is chosen at the start of the level) and the Colombian Dodgers. This weapon is required for the A BOX FULL OF SHARP OBJECTS achievement.
Rare, being usable only if found via Weapon Spawns or if the Bodyguard Technique is chosen.

p: The Knife has a special property that allows it to sometimes kill an enemy if the knife is thrown at them. Thrown knives that are fatal cannot be retrieved, as they will be stuck inside the corpse. A thrown knife can be retrieved as normal if it does not kill the person that it hits.

In Hotline Miami, the Knife is amongst some of the most common melee weapons, being used by Mobsters and often found on the ground. This is the fastest melee weapon in the game. By using the Dennis Mask, the player starts the level with a knife. The Knife is required for the Always On Top and Knife For Pros achievements.

weapons.name: M16
weapons.desc: The M16, also known as the Machine Gun, is a weapon appearing in both Hotline Miami and Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

p: The M16 is a very common firearm in Hotline Miami, seeing extensive use from Mobsters and the Miami Police Department. It boasts a high rate of fire, accuracy stat and one of the largest magazine sizes in the game (being beaten only by the Uzi, Silenced Uzi and the MP5). This weapon is required for the Guns For Show achievement.

In Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, this weapon makes a return, although with some slight changes as it now possesses a smaller 20-round magazine. It is also the third most accurate fully automatic weapon in the game (beaten by the Flamethrower and Heavy Machine Gun). Like in Hotline Miami, this weapon is seen on the hands of Mobsters (although less often due to the introduction of the Kalashnikov) and the Miami Police Department, and it is also in service during the Hawaiian Conflict, being one of the weapons The Soldier can use if the Player picks it at the start of the level, being one of the two firearm choices available by default.

stats.Real-world model: Colt M16A3 (Unlock Image), Colt M733 (In-game Sprite)

weapons.name: Machete
weapons.desc: The Machete is a weapon in Hotline Miami and Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

p: In Hotline Miami, The Machete is an unlockable weapon, meaning it can spawn randomly once it has been unlocked. This is the 4th weapon you receive. This weapon is required for the Always On Top, Knife For Pros and I Got New Friends achievements.

In Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, the Machete is commonly used by the Colombians and the Soldiers, although Beard is unable to pick the machetes dropped by them. Manny Pardo and The Son (characters that can wield the weapon) both have unique executions with the Machete. Manny Pardo will slit the throat of his victim (similarly to the Butterfly Knife) while The Son will hack off the victim's head (similar to how Jacket executes his victims with the machete, but much slower.)
Execution animation may be slow depending on which character the Player is using

weapons.name: Magnum
weapons.desc: The Magnum is a weapon that appears in Hotline Miami and Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

p: This weapon has two unique properties: the ability to penetrate multiple enemies (with the exception of bosses and Heavies) without stopping, and the ability to deal 2 points of damage. In comparison, all other firearms deal two points of damage.

In Hotline Miami, the Magnum is an unlockable weapon, meaning it can randomly spawn once you have unlocked it. It is the third weapon you receive. The Magnum is not affected by the Rami Mask's powerup. This weapon is required for the I Got New Friends and Guns For Show achievements. The Magnum in the first game does not deal bonus damage against thug enemies.

In Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, it is first seen in Final Cut being dual-wielded by the SWAT Chief, but they cannot be used by the Pig Butcher. Magnums appear during several cutscenes, including one where Manny Pardo kills Tony with one, but they remain unusable until Release, where they are held by security guards and prisoners. This is the weapon is used to kill The Zebra in Apocalypse, and The Swans in Death Wish. This iteration of the Magnum shares many similarities with the Hotline Miami version, but it has inferior accuracy. Additionally Prisoner, and Police/Guard Heavies will die after two Magnum shots, however any other Fat enemy type will die in 5 shots.
Deals 2 points of Damage (with the exception of non-Guard heavy enemies)
Can shoot through multiple targets with a single shot (with the exception of heavy and boss enemies)

weapons.name: MP5
weapons.desc: The MP5 is a weapon appearing in Hotline Miami and Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

p: The MP5 is an unlockable weapon, meaning it may randomly spawn once unlocked; this is the 13th weapon you receive. The MP5 will always spawn on the second floor in Clean Hit, it is located on a balcony close to where you end up by climbing through the window. It is also seen being dual-wielded by the Police Chief in Assault and by The Father in Showdown. The MP5 is not affected by the Rami Mask perk. This weapon is required for the Guns For Show and I Got New Friends achievements.

The MP5 makes a return in Wrong Number, where it is usable in its dual-wielded form by Mark and The Son (using his Bloodline technique). By holding the Throw Weapon button, those characters can perform a special ability where they point the MP5s to their sides instead of straight ahead. This weapon also appears in the Hawaiian Conflict, being used by Soviet Heavies and Jacket, although it is unusable by The Soldier. This weapon is required for the A BOX FULL OF SHARP OBJECTS achievement.
Extremely large magazine capacity, even larger when dual wielded

stats.Found: Weapon Spawn, Second Floor in Clean Hit, Third Floor in Assault, Showdown, Mark, The Son, Soviet Heavy Soldier

weapons.name: Ninja Star
weapons.desc: The Ninja Star or the Shuriken is a weapon that appears exclusively in Hotline Miami.

p: The Ninja Star is an unlockable weapon, meaning it will only spawn once it has been unlocked; It is the 11th weapon you receive. This weapon is required for the Pitcher and I Got New Friends achievements. This throwable is a one-time use weapon, as it disappears once it has killed its target.

weapons.name: Pistol
weapons.desc: if you are looking for the usable pistol in Wrong Number, see 9mm. The Pistol is an unique weapon briefly seen in Hotline Miami and Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

p: In Hotline Miami The Pistol is briefly seen in Showdown, The Father uses it to commit suicide once he has been defeated, and Jacket then uses it to kill The Grandfather.

In Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number The pistol is briefly seen in the prologue for First Trial, seen on the evidence table along with Jacket's blood-stained jacket, the Richard, Tony and Aubrey masks, along the Trophy used to kill the Panthers and The Bodyguard.

weapons.name: Pool Cue
weapons.desc: The Pool Cue is a weapon in seen exclusively in Hotline Miami.

p: In Hotline Miami, the Pool Cue is a weapon that can only spawn in predetermined locations. It has an unique feature where it breaks once you kill a common enemy with it, turning into a Broken Pool Cue. Killing Dogs with the Pool Cue does not reduce its durability, and the Broken Pool Cue disappears once an enemy is killed with it. This is one of the only weapons in the game to have two unique Execution animations tied to it; one for the unbroken cue, and one for the broken one. This weapon is required for the Always On Top and Knife For Pros achievements. Note that you must kill and execute an enemy with the unbroken and broken version of the Pool Cue for those achievements.

stats.Found: Second floor in Decadence, Second floor in Tension, First floor in Full House, First floor in Crackdown

weapons.name: Pot
weapons.desc: The Pot is a weapon that appears in Hotline Miami and Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

p: It is a steel pot filled with boiling water that produces steam particles. Upon attacking with it, the boiling water will be expelled from the pot and will burn common enemies if they are caught in its radius.

In Hotline Miami, the Pot is a weapon that can only spawn in one predetermined location. It is one of the only weapons in the game to have two unique executions tied to it. This weapon is required for the Always On Top and Knife For Pros achievements. Note that you must kill an enemy with the full pot and the empty pot for those achievements. This weapon is often mistaken for the Frying Pan.
Extremely rare, being only found in one level and the Level Editor
Lengthy execution animation if still full

stats.Found: Second floor in Overdose, Level Editor

weapons.name: Scissors
weapons.desc: The Scissors are a throwable weapon seen in Hotline Miami. Its a normal pair of scissors with red handles and grey blades.

p: The Scissors are an unlockable weapon, meaning they will only spawn once unlocked; It is the penultimate weapon you receive. The Scissors are quite similar to the Ninja Star, as it is a one-use weapon and disappears once it has killed its target. It is possible to see these scissors in Jacket's apartment in the prologue of some Chapters, next to the newspaper clippings. This weapon is required for the Pitcher, Always On Top and I Got New Friends achievements.
Extra points for killing and executing Cons:

weapons.name: Shard Blade
weapons.desc: The Shard Blade is a weapon featured in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. It is a shiv fashioned out of a piece of broken glass.

p: The Shard Blade is a weapon found only in Release, being found on the hands of Prisoners. It is very similar to the Knife, recycling many of its animations, although unlike the Knife, the Shard Blade is a very fragile weapon, as it breaks once it is thrown away or if a Door passes over it, and it cannot kill enemies if you throw it at them. This weapon is required for the A BOX FULL OF SHARP OBJECTS achievement.
Extremely rare, Hotline Miami 2 exclusive
Breaks if thrown away or if crushed by a door

weapons.name: Shotgun
weapons.desc: The Shotgun is a weapon seen in Hotline Miami and Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

p: This is the most common firearm in the series, seeing extensive use from most factions across both games. The Shotgun is unique, as it is one of the two weapons (the other being the Sniper Rifle) that has a short delay between shots, as it is a pump action firearm and it needs to chamber a new shell once it has been fired.

The Shotgun is an extremely common weapon, being seen on the hands of Mobsters and the Miami Police Department. It is a very powerful firearm, having 6 to 12 projectiles in an arc appear per shot fired, and a moderate rate of fire, being beaten only by the Double Barrel in terms of damage and projectiles. The Shotgun is required to progress in certain parts of the game, as the bomb room in Tension cannot be bypassed without the use of it, and it is also one of the only weapons that can kill Thugs and The Producer (even if the Player has the Tony Mask). This weapon is required for the Guns For Show achievement.

This weapon makes a return in Hotline Miami 2, where it is also abundant, being not only used by Mobsters and the Miami Police Department, but also Gang Members, Colombians, Guards, Prisoners and the Hallucinatory Demons. A guaranteed Shotgun spawn can be found in the trunk of Manny Pardo's car in Homicide, and he has an unique animation for 'flipping' it if the Player quickly looks in another direction, although this is completely cosmetic. The Shotgun has an unique attribute, where the rate of fire is dependent on the character the Player is currently using.

stats.Found: Weapon Spawn, Mobster, Police, Gang, Colombian, Guard, Prisoner, Decadence, Homicide

weapons.name: Silenced Pistol
weapons.desc: The Silenced Pistol (Silencer internally) is a weapon in Hotline Miami and Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. It is a pistol fitted with a silencer, meaning enemies will be unable to hear it's gunshots.

p: In Hotline Miami, the Silenced Pistol is an unlockable weapon, meaning it may spawn randomly it has been unlocked; this is the last weapon you receive. Additionally, Mobsters are seen wielding the pistol exclusively in Deadline. This weapon is required for the Guns For Show and I Got New Friends achievements.

In the sequel, the Silenced Pistol makes a return, where it is now one of the more common ranged weapons in the game, being commonly carried by Mobsters and Colombians. The Silenced Pistol also sees use by The Henchman, as he starts the level No Mercy equipped with one. The Silenced Pistol has a faster rate of fire when the Player is using it as Richter. This weapon is required for the A BOX FULL OF SHARP OBJECTS and ASSASSIN'S CRED achievements.
Slow rate of fire (unless playing as Richter)

weapons.name: Silenced Uzi
weapons.desc: The Silenced Uzi is a weapon featured in Hotline Miami and Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

p: In Hotline Miami, this weapon is first seen on the hands of Richter, and he uses it to kill Girlfriend and severely wound Jacket. It also makes an appearance in Assault, where it is resting on the third floor on an evidence table alongside Richter's belongings, unable to be picked up and used. If the Player picks the Richter Mask, they will start the level off with a Silenced UZI. This weapon is required for the Guns For Show achievement. This weapon functions exactly like the UZI, except for the silenced weapon property.

In the sequel, this weapon makes a return in the Level Editor, where it can only be used by Richter and Jacket. This iteration of the Silenced UZI has a nerfed firerate, going from 1800 RPM to only 900.
Rate of fire is halved in Hotline Miami 2

stats.Fire rate / speed: 1,800 Rounds Per Minute (HM1) 900 Rounds Per Minute (HM2)

weapons.name: Skateboard
weapons.desc: The Skateboard is a weapon in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

p: This weapon is only available in the level No Mercy, where it can be picked up by The Henchman shortly after entering the building. This weapon is required for the A BOX FULL OF SHARP OBJECTS achievement.
Extremely rare, Hotline Miami 2 exclusive

weapons.name: Skorpion
weapons.desc: The Skorpion is a weapon featured in Hotline Miami and Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number (although unusable by the player in the second game).

p: In Hotline Miami, the Skorpion is an unlockable weapon, meaning that it will randomly spawn once it is unlocked; This is the 6th weapon you receive. This weapon is required for the I Got New Friends and Guns For Show achievements.

In Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, the Skorpion can only be found on arcade machines, and in a display cabinet located in The Henchman's home, all of those being unusable. The Skorpion otherwise has a spiritual successor in the FAMAE.
Runs out of ammo quickly due to the very fast rate of fire

weapons.name: Sledgehammer
weapons.desc: The Sledgehammer is a weapon featured exclusively in Hotline Miami.

p: It's a large hammer often used for demolition or combat purposes; It has a similar appearance to the Hammer; a wooden handle and a black head.

The Sledgehammer is an unlockable weapon, meaning that it will only spawn once you have unlocked it; It is the 10th weapon you receive. This weapon is required for the Always On Top, Knife For Pros and I Got New Friends achievements.
Longest attack animation out of all melee weapons

weapons.name: Taser
weapons.desc: The Taser is a weapon that appears in Hotline Miami and Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, it is an electroshock weapon made for incapacitating rather than killing victims.

p: In Hotline Miami, this weapon is exclusively seen in Assault, being used by the Inspectors. However, Jacket is unable to pick up the weapon from fallen Inspectors.

In Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number the Taser returns and it is usable in a few levels. The first level where this weapon is seen is in Final Cut, where the Pig Butcher can pick it up from fallen Inspectors. It's second appearance is in Caught, where Manny Pardo can obtain one via the same method. This weapon is required for the A BOX FULL OF SHARP OBJECTS achievement, but beware that it only counts for the achievement if you use the weapon in Final Cut.
Extremely rare, only usable in Hotline Miami 2

weapons.name: Throwing Knife
weapons.desc: The Throwing Knife is a weapon featured in Hotline Miami and Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. This weapon has many appearances; three different variants being used by The Bodyguard and the Biker respectively. This is one of the two weapons the Biker can use, the other one being the Cleaver.

p: In Hotline Miami, the Throwing Knife is first found in Showdown, where they are dropped by The Bodyguard after Jacket kills her. They are used to maim and disarm The Father. This is the only time Jacket ever uses the throwing knives.

Later on, Biker starts all of his chapters with three Throwing Knives that are used as his only means of ranged combat. If they are thrown at a wall, they will get stuck and can be retrieved. However, it cannot be retrieved if you successfully kill an enemy with it.
The Player is granted three throwing knives Cons:
Cannot be retrieved once it kills an enemy

weapons.name: Toothbrush
weapons.desc: The Toothbrush is a weapon seen in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. It is a shiv fashioned out of a green, prison-issued toothbrush.

p: This weapon only appears in the level Release, being exclusively used by the Prisoners. This weapon is a one-time use, meaning it cannot be retrieved from your victim once used. Curiously, the Toothbrush does not knock down enemies if you throw it at them. This weapon is required for the A BOX FULL OF SHARP OBJECTS achievement.
Extremely rare, Hotline Miami 2 exclusive

weapons.name: Trophy
weapons.desc: The Trophy is an unique weapon available in Hotline Miami and seen in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, It is a sharp, golden decorative trophy.

p: The Trophy appears only in Showdown, it is located on the right side of the second floor, and it's there as the weapon you must use to kill the Panthers and incapacitate The Bodyguard
In Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number the Trophy makes a brief appearance on the evidence table during the prologue to First Trial, Unlike its first iteration, it is not usable.

weapons.name: Uzi
weapons.desc: The Uzi is a weapon that appears in Hotline Miami and Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. There is a silenced version of this weapon.

p: In Hotline Miami, The UZI is an unlockable weapon, meaning it will only spawn once it has been unlocked; This is the 9th weapon you receive. The UZI can be seen in Clean Hit, where it is wielded by the Waiter enemies on the first floor. This weapon is required for the Guns For Show and I Got New Friends achievements.

In Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, The Uzi has been made more common, being used by Gang Members and the Demons during Apocalypse. Blue Lips is seen carrying this weapon during Blood Money. This iteration of the Uzi has a much lower rate of fire, being lowered from 1,800 RPM to 900 RPM. This weapon is required for the A BOX FULL OF SHARP OBJECTS achievement.
Quickly runs out of ammo in Hotline Miami
Rate of fire is halved in Hotline Miami 2

weapons.name: Acid
weapons.desc: Acid is a weapon found exclusively in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

p: This weapon can only be seen in Withdrawal, it is located in the meth labs. Acid is a very fragile weapon, meaning it will disappear once used, regardless of if it hits its target or not. It will also disappear if a Door hits it while its opening. This weapon is required for the A BOX FULL OF SHARP OBJECTS achievement.
Extremely rare, Hotline Miami 2 exclusive
Fragile; disappears once broken against enemies or walls or crushed by a door

weapons.name: FAMAE
weapons.desc: The FAMAE is a weapon in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

p: The FAMAE can be primarily seen being wielded by the Colombians. This weapon is very similar to the Skorpion featured in Hotline Miami, having the same magazine capacity and a slightly slower rate of fire, However, it possesses a lower accuracy stat and it is much more common than the Skorpion. Curiously, when this weapon is dropped by hiding Colombians, it will get four more rounds in its magazine. This weapon is required for the A BOX FULL OF SHARP OBJECTS achievement.

weapons.name: Flamethrower
weapons.desc: The Flamethrower is a weapon featured Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number'. It is one of the three weapons exclusively available for The Soldier.

p: The Flamethrower is seen exclusively in the Hawaiian Conflict, where it is one of the weapons The Soldier can use if the Player decides to take it at the start of a level; This weapon is only unlocked once Casualties is completed. The Flamethrower is an insanely powerful weapon, boasting the highest magazine size out of any weapon in the game and a perfect accuracy stat. Once the starting ammunition is depleted, each ammunition pickup will only give 40 ammo. This weapon is required for the A BOX FULL OF SHARP OBJECTS achievement.
Largest ammunition capacity of any firearm
Cannot shoot through windows, even if they are broken

weapons.name: Mendoza
weapons.desc: The Mendoza is a weapon that appears in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

p: The Mendoza is a firearm that sees extensive use from the Colombians. This weapon is very similar to the MP5 seen in Hotline Miami, sporting the same magazine size, although with a lower rate of fire and a slightly decreased accuracy stat; It is the 4th most accurate weapon in the game, being beaten only by the M16, Flamethrower and Sniper Rifle. Besides being commonly found with Colombians, The Son has the option to use a Mendoza during Blood Money if the Player decides to pick the weapon up at the start of the level. This weapon is required for the A BOX FULL OF SHARP OBJECTS achievement.

weapons.name: RPG
weapons.desc: The RPG was a weapon featured in Super Carnage.

p: The RPG would have functioned similarly to a stereotypical "Missile Launcher"; a long weapon that can fire a rocket (which would have had a smoke trail following it), and it would explode as soon as it hit an object (i.e Enemies, Walls, Furniture).

weapons.name: Nail Gun
weapons.desc: The Nail Gun is a weapon seen in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

p: The Nailgun is available exclusively to Jake when he is using the Irvin Mask; It is only unlocked when Hard News is completed. Similarly to the Silenced Pistol, this weapon will not alert enemies when fired, and it also has a special property that allows it to ignore destroyable props such as meth labs, arcades and computer monitors. Despite these attributes, the Nail Gun has the worst accuracy out of all the firearms, and has a very slow rate of fire.
Projectiles ignore destroyable props Cons:
Extremely rare, Hotline Miami 2 exclusive

weapons.name: Sniper Rifle
weapons.desc: The Sniper Rifle is a weapon seen in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. It is one of the three weapons that is exclusively available for The Soldier.

p: The Sniper Rifle is seen only in the Hawaiian Conflict, being available only for The Soldier if the Player decides to take it at the start of the level; It is only available once Stronghold is completed. This is one of the most accurate and powerful weapon in the game (tied with the Flamethrower), as it can kill Thugs with one shot. However, similarly to the Shotgun, this weapon has a short delay between firing rounds as it is a bolt-action rifle, meaning it needs to be 'reloaded' after every shot. The Sniper Rifle also has a special property that increases the viewing range of the Player (similarly to the George Mask). This weapon is required for the A BOX FULL OF SHARP OBJECTS achievement.
Delay between shots, as it needs to chamber a new round after every bullet

weapons.name: Minigun
weapons.desc: The Minigun is a weapon seen in the Super Carnage prototype, and it can also be seen in Comic #5 of the Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number Digital Comics, being used by Beard in the Hawaiian Conflict. Prototype-only (Super Carnage); not usable in either released game.

p: This weapon is one of the 5 ranged weapons available to the Player in the prototype. It has the highest rate of fire out of any weapon and it will absolutely annihilate anything that enters its path.

weapons.name: Grenade
weapons.desc: The Grenade is a weapon available in the Super Carnage prototype.

p: The Grenade is one of the three weapons available in the room where the Player character spawns. It has a fuse of 5 seconds, and a massive blast radius. This is the only explosive featured in Super Carnage.

weapons.name: Plank
weapons.desc: The Plank is a weapon that is included in the Super Carnage prototype. It's a wooden board meant to be used as a construction material.

p: This weapon can be found on the floor alongside the other melee weapons featured in the prototype. It does not have any unique attributes or properties.

weapons.name: Nunchaku
weapons.desc: The Nunchaku is a melee weapon exclusive to Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. Jake can use nunchucks while wearing the Dallas mask (Inner Warrior), which otherwise blocks picking up weapons.

p: Listed as a Hotline Miami 2 exclusive melee weapon on the wiki Weapons page.
